# Dialog reference scope

`sources.json` pins unchanged AndroidX `a095da93f8e98dea8748ceed79ea8427aade245f`, MDC Android `60ff09436d5d477a4b9d02940f31eb01e1250620` and Android 15 resource sources, with SHA-256 for every file. Original license headers are retained.

The web AlertDialog body follows AndroidX `AlertDialogContent`: Surface with no supplied border or shadow elevation, zero default tonal elevation, SurfaceContainerHigh, 24dp container padding, 16dp icon/title bottom spacing, 24dp text bottom spacing, and a centered title when an icon is present. Default actions use the shared TextButton component. The precision-pointer opt-in sizing branch, the full original FlowRow/composable measure tree, compiler behavior and native raster are not executed by this check.

AndroidX `Dialog` owns a platform window and inherits its host window theme. It does not prescribe the former web component's anisotropic scale, vertical displacement or spatial spring. The web window default is the concrete MDC `Material3.Dialog` theme (inherited by Material3Expressive): its original XML enters with alpha 0→1 and uniform scale 0.8→1, Medium4=400ms and emphasized-decelerate (0.1,0.7,0.1,1); exit is alpha-only 1→0, Short3=150ms and emphasized-accelerate (0.3,0,0.8,0.2). The original dialog token supplies scrim opacity 0.32. Android 15 resources show that other host window themes can instead use translation; they are retained as evidence of the platform boundary, not as the web default.

`test/browser/dialog-parity.mjs` checks source integrity, derives motion numbers and cubic controls directly from the unchanged XML, and compares actual browser half-time opacity/scale. It verifies retained DOM and modal ownership, trusted actions, focus, reentry, outside gestures, native window closure, reconnect/dispose, shared body scroll locks, reduced motion and actual responsive showcase controls. This does not execute Android Animation/PathInterpolator/window-manager code, prove exact native Float frame sampling, or claim all Android/OS window themes look identical.

Date/Time picker wrappers share the modal controller. Their full calendar/dial/input/range layout, selection, keyboard semantics, locale model and native trajectories remain separate pending work. In particular the old calendar's 328dp container/36dp selection/40dp reservation differ from DatePickerModalTokens and should not be mistaken for complete DatePicker parity.
